aiPolicyMetaDescription: Read how Digitaltableteur uses AI-assisted tools, the safeguards applied and your rights under EU law.
aiPolicyIntro: Digitaltableteur uses AI-assisted tools in the website assistant and in parts of design, development and editorial work. This statement explains the intended uses, limits, data flow and safeguards. It is a transparency notice, not a legal certification or a promise that every AI output is error-free.
aiPolicyAssistantScope: Donny is an AI assistant that answers questions about published Digitaltableteur site content, services, work and design-system topics. Replies are generated automatically and are not reviewed by a person before you receive them.
aiPolicyAssistantBoundary: Donny does not rank or profile people, make employment or eligibility decisions, infer emotions or biometric traits, provide legal, medical or financial advice or make binding commitments about price, availability, delivery or contracts. A person must confirm any proposal or commitment.
aiPolicyAssistantData: When you send a message, the text and recent conversation context are sent to the configured model service, using an OpenAI model directly or through Vercel AI Gateway. A temporary browser copy is kept in sessionStorage until you clear it or close the tab. Do not submit sensitive personal data.
aiPolicyPrincipleHuman: Human accountability: Published work and client deliverables receive substantive human review before publication or delivery. Live website-chat replies are automatic and are not pre-reviewed.
aiPolicyPrincipleTransparency: Transparency: The AI tools used in each project are documented and disclosed to clients upon request.
aiPolicyPrinciplePrivacy: Privacy first: Personal data is minimized, masked or excluded where the task allows. Training, reuse, retention and transfer settings are checked for the actual provider account and use.
aiPolicyPrincipleQuality: Quality assurance: AI is used as an assistive tool, not a replacement for professional expertise and judgment.
aiPolicyUseCaseDesign: Design exploration: generating alternative layouts, color palettes or visual concepts for internal review. All AI suggestions are evaluated and refined by experienced designers before implementation.
aiPolicyUseCaseContent: Editorial assistance: drafting article outlines, alt text descriptions, meta descriptions or translation suggestions. All content is fact-checked, edited for accuracy and approved by a human editor.
aiPolicyUseCaseCode: Code assistance: generating code snippets, documentation or refactoring suggestions using GitHub Copilot or similar tools. All code is reviewed, tested and validated before deployment.
aiPolicyUseCaseOperations: Quality assurance: analyzing anonymized support tickets, error logs and telemetry data to identify accessibility issues, performance bottlenecks or user experience improvements.
aiPolicyUseCaseChat: Website chat: Donny uses an OpenAI model, directly or through Vercel AI Gateway, to answer visitor questions from site context. The interface identifies the system as AI before the visitor sends a message.
aiPolicyNotUsedBody: AI is not used for: automated decision-making that affects your rights; high-risk applications as defined by the EU AI Act; final design deliverables without human review; legal, financial or medical advice; or making hiring or business decisions about individuals.
aiPolicyProvidersIntro: Provider selection depends on the feature or project. The live website assistant uses an OpenAI model directly or through Vercel AI Gateway. Internal work may also use the tools listed below. Contract, retention, sub-processor and transfer settings must be checked for the actual account and use before personal data is processed:
aiPolicyProviderOpenAI: OpenAI: model processing for the website assistant and selected internal drafting tasks. The exact model and routing can change with the deployment configuration.
aiPolicyProviderGitHub: GitHub Copilot: for selected code suggestions and development assistance, subject to the settings and terms of the account in use.
aiPolicyProviderAnthropic: Anthropic (Claude): for selected internal reasoning or content-analysis tasks, subject to the settings and terms of the account in use.
aiPolicyProvidersFooter: A provider name alone is not proof of compliance. Digitaltableteur reviews the relevant service terms, data-processing terms, transfer mechanism, sub-processors, data-use controls and retention settings for the intended use.
aiPolicyDataItem1: Only necessary prompts: only the minimum information required for the specific task is shared
aiPolicyDataItem2: Personal data minimized: client workflows remove or mask identifiers where the task allows; website-chat text is sent as entered, so visitors are told not to submit sensitive personal data
aiPolicyDataItem3: Training and reuse controls: the applicable account settings and provider terms must prevent submitted client or visitor data from being used for model training unless a separate lawful, disclosed decision permits it
aiPolicyDataItem4: Sensitive data excluded: confidential business information, credentials and special-category personal data must not be entered into public or website AI tools
aiPolicyDataFooter: For website chat, Digitaltableteur does not write the transcript to an application database in the chat route. The browser keeps a temporary sessionStorage copy until you clear it or close the tab. The configured model service processes the submitted text and may keep service or abuse-monitoring records under the applicable account terms.
aiPolicySafeguardHumanReview: Human review: published work and client deliverables are reviewed for substance, accuracy, sources, bias and appropriateness. Live assistant replies are instead bounded by interface warnings, system rules, source-grounding controls and a route to report a problem.
aiPolicySafeguardDataMinimisation: Data minimization: prompts are truncated, masked or sampled so that individuals cannot be identified. Technical and organizational measures are applied to protect privacy.
aiPolicySafeguardVendorReview: Vendor review: only providers that offer EU-grade security, data processing agreements (DPAs) and compliance with GDPR and emerging AI regulations are used.
aiPolicySafeguardMonitoring: Monitoring and auditing: logs of AI usage in client projects are maintained and periodic reviews are conducted to ensure compliance with Digitaltableteur's policies and standards.
aiPolicySafeguardTraining: Team training: Digitaltableteur staff receives guidance on responsible AI use, prompt engineering and identifying AI limitations or biases.
aiPolicyLimitationsBody: AI systems can produce inaccurate, incomplete or biased outputs and can miss context. Donny's live replies are not professional advice and are not reviewed before display. Verify important information using the linked site source or contact Petri before relying on it. Published work and client deliverables follow a separate human editorial review.
aiPolicyRightInformation: Right to information: you can ask Digitaltableteur which AI systems were used in your project or to process your data at any time. A clear explanation will be provided.
aiPolicyRightObjection: Right to object: you may request that AI-assisted tools are avoided in your project. Feasibility will be confirmed and the alternative workflow documented. Some projects may require additional time or cost adjustments.
aiPolicyRightErasure: Right to erasure: if AI tools processed personal data related to you, you can request deletion. Data will be erased in accordance with Digitaltableteur's retention policies or contractual obligations.
aiPolicyRightHumanReview: Right to human review: if you believe an AI-generated output adversely affected you, you can request human review and challenge the outcome.
aiPolicyRightsFooter: To exercise these rights, email mail@digitaltableteur.com or use the channels listed in the privacy policy. Digitaltableteur will respond within one month.
aiPolicyChangesBody: As AI technology and regulations evolve, this statement may be updated. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Clients and visitors are encouraged to review this statement periodically.
aiPolicyContactBody: For questions, requests or concerns about this AI use & transparency statement, contact: mail@digitaltableteur.com or +358 45 657 4469
privacyPolicyIntro: Digitaltableteur respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal data. This policy explains what information is collected, how it is used and your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and other applicable data protection laws.
privacyPolicyControllerBody:
Petri Lahdelma (Digitaltableteur)
Helsinki, Finland
Email: mail@digitaltableteur.com
privacyPolicyPurposeBody: This Privacy Policy describes how Digitaltableteur collects and processes personal data about potential clients, website visitors, contact form users and newsletter subscribers. This data is collected to respond to inquiries, provide design and development services, improve the website and communicate about current offerings. The aim is to be transparent about these practices.
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectTitle: What data is collected and how is it used?
privacyPolicyContactFormIntro: If you get in touch via the forms or email, the following is collected:
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem1: Your name and contact information (email, phone number if provided)
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem2: Message content and any attachments you send
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem3: Information relevant to your inquiry or project request
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem4: Communication history between you and Digitaltableteur
privacyPolicyContactFormUsage: This data is used to respond to your inquiries, process project requests, provide services and maintain the business relationship with you. Digitaltableteur has a legitimate interest to process this data based on your direct contact and the need to manage customer relationships.
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsIntro: When you visit this website, the following is collected automatically:
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsItem1: Technical data (IP address, browser type, device information)
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsItem2: Usage data (pages visited, time spent, navigation patterns)
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsItem3: Referral source (how you found this site)
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsUsage: This data is used with your consent (via cookie banner) to analyze site usage, improve user experience and optimize services. You can withdraw consent at any time through your browser settings or by clearing this site's cookies.
privacyPolicyChatBody: When you use Donny, the message text and recent conversation context are sent to the configured model service to generate a reply. The chat route does not write the transcript to a Digitaltableteur application database. Your browser keeps a temporary sessionStorage copy until you clear the conversation or close the tab. The service provider may retain operational or abuse-monitoring records under the applicable account terms. Do not submit sensitive personal data.
privacyPolicyLegalBasisBody: Digitaltableteur processes your personal data based on: (1) Your consent when you submit forms or accept cookies; (2) Legitimate interest in managing business relationships, improving services and responding to inquiries; (3) Contractual necessity when providing services you requested; (4) Legal obligations where required by Finnish or EU law.
privacyPolicySharingIntro: Digitaltableteur does not sell your personal data. Data is only shared with trusted service providers necessary to operate the website and services:
privacyPolicySharingItem1: Resend: for delivering contact form submissions
privacyPolicySharingItem2: Vercel: for website hosting and analytics
privacyPolicySharingItem3: Google Analytics: for website usage statistics (with your consent)
privacyPolicySharingItem4: OpenAI, directly or through Vercel AI Gateway: to process website-chat messages and generate replies
privacyPolicySharingFooter: All service providers are bound by data processing agreements and comply with GDPR requirements. Your data is not shared outside these purposes unless required by law or public authorities.
privacyPolicyTransfersBody: Some service providers (Vercel, OpenAI) may process data outside the European Economic Area. Lawful transfers are ensured through appropriate safeguards including standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission, adequacy decisions or equivalent mechanisms compliant with GDPR Article 46.
privacyPolicyCookiesIntro: This website uses cookies to improve your browsing experience. Cookies are small text files stored on your device. Some are necessary for the website to function; others help reveal usage patterns.
privacyPolicyCookiesTypes: When you access this website, your consent is asked to store the following cookies:
privacyPolicyCookiesItem1: Necessary cookies: required for basic site functionality (cookie consent choice, session management)
privacyPolicyCookiesItem2: Analytics cookies: Google Analytics to measure visitor behavior, traffic sources and popular pages. This helps improve the site.
privacyPolicyCookiesItem3: Performance cookies: to monitor site speed and identify technical issues
privacyPolicyCookiesControl: You can control cookies through the banner or your browser settings. Disabling non-essential cookies may limit some features but won't prevent basic site access. For more details, see the Cookie Policy.
privacyPolicyRetentionTitle: How long is your data stored?
privacyPolicyRetentionBody: Personal data is retained only as long as necessary for the purposes described or as required by law. The browser copy of an AI-chat transcript lasts for the current tab session or until you clear it; the chat route does not create a server-side transcript database. Provider operational or abuse-monitoring records follow the configured account terms. Contact form submissions are kept for up to 2 years or until you request deletion. Analytics data is anonymized after 14 months. Data no longer needed is regularly reviewed and deleted. If you have an active business relationship with Digitaltableteur, relevant data is retained for the duration of that relationship plus any legally required retention period.
privacyPolicyYourRightsTitle: What rights do you have concerning your data?
privacyPolicyYourRightsIntro: Under GDPR, you have the following rights:
privacyPolicyRightAccess: Right to access: request a copy of the personal data held about you
privacyPolicyRightRectification: Right to rectification: request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data
privacyPolicyRightErasure: Right to erasure: request deletion of your personal data ("right to be forgotten")
privacyPolicyRightRestriction: Right to restrict processing: request limits on how your data is used
privacyPolicyRightPortability: Right to data portability: receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format
privacyPolicyRightObject: Right to object: object to processing based on legitimate interests or for marketing purposes
privacyPolicyRightWithdraw: Right to withdraw consent: withdraw your consent at any time (e.g., for cookies or newsletters)
privacyPolicyRightsExercise: To exercise any of these rights, contact mail@digitaltableteur.com. Digitaltableteur will respond within one month.
privacyPolicyRightsComplaint: If you believe your data has not been handled properly, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Finnish Data Protection Ombudsman (www.tietosuoja.fi) or your local data protection authority.
privacyPolicySecurityIntro: All personal data is considered confidential and protected with appropriate security measures:
privacyPolicySecurityItem1: Access controls: only authorized personnel can access personal data when necessary for their work
privacyPolicySecurityItem2: Encryption: data is transmitted over HTTPS and stored securely
privacyPolicySecurityItem3: Network security: the infrastructure and partners in use apply industry-standard protections against unauthorized access, loss or alteration
privacyPolicySecurityItem4: Service provider agreements: all third-party processors are contractually bound to maintain confidentiality and security standards
privacyPolicySecurityFooter: While every effort is made to protect your data, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure. Security practices are continuously reviewed and updated.
privacyPolicyChangesBody: This Privacy Policy may be updated as the website, services and practices improve. Any changes will be posted on this page with an updated "Last updated" date. You are encouraged to review this policy periodically. Continued use of this website after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
privacyPolicyContactBody: For questions, requests or concerns about this Privacy Policy or your personal data, contact: mail@digitaltableteur.com or +358 45 657 4469
accessibilityIntro: Digitaltableteur is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. Everyone should be able to access this website and its services, regardless of ability. The user experience is continually improved for all visitors and relevant accessibility standards are applied.
accessibilityConformanceBody: The target is Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 Level AA. Full conformance requires every applicable Level A and AA criterion to be met across complete pages and processes.
accessibilityConformanceLevel: Current status: Full conformance has not yet been verified. Automated checks and targeted interaction tests do not establish conformance on their own. Assistive-technology, media and document verification remain necessary.
accessibilityMeasuresIntro: Digitaltableteur takes the following measures to ensure accessibility:
accessibilityMeasuresItem1: Integrate accessibility into design and development processes
accessibilityMeasuresItem2: Use automated and manual testing tools (axe-core, screen readers) throughout development
accessibilityMeasuresItem3: Train team members on accessibility best practices and WCAG guidelines
accessibilityMeasuresItem4: Include people with disabilities in user testing when possible
accessibilityMeasuresItem5: Regularly review and update accessibility practices
accessibilityStandardsBody: The W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 Level AA serve as the technical accessibility target.
accessibilityTechnicalIntro: The accessibility of this website relies on the following technologies:
accessibilityTechnicalItem1: HTML5: semantic markup for proper document structure
accessibilityTechnicalItem2: CSS3: for visual presentation and responsive design
accessibilityTechnicalItem3: JavaScript: for interactive components with ARIA attributes
accessibilityTechnicalItem4: WAI-ARIA 1.2: to enhance accessibility of dynamic content
accessibilityCompatibilityTitle: Compatibility with browsers and assistive technology
accessibilityCompatibilityBody: Browser-rendered semantics, keyboard interactions, reflow and text spacing are tested programmatically. End-to-end compatibility with NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver and voice-control software has not yet been confirmed for this release.
accessibilityLimitationsIntro: Despite best efforts, some areas of this website may not be fully accessible:
accessibilityLimitationsItem1: The Garage Junction promotional video has audible sound but no caption track. Captions and audio-description requirements for published videos still need a content-level review.
accessibilityLimitationsItem2: Older PDF documents may not meet current accessibility standards. These files are being remediated.
accessibilityLimitationsItem3: Some complex interactive features are still being improved for full keyboard and screen reader support.
accessibilityLimitationsFooter: These limitations are being actively addressed. If you encounter a specific barrier, please get in touch for assistance or an alternative.
accessibilityShortcomingsIntro: Full conformance cannot yet be claimed. The following areas still need end-to-end verification and any confirmed barriers will be documented and corrected.
accessibilityShortcomingsItem1: Captions, transcripts and audio descriptions need a content-level review for every published video.
accessibilityShortcomingsItem2: Downloadable documents and third-party booking or media services need separate accessibility verification.
accessibilityShortcomingsItem3: Dynamic announcements and complete contact and chat flows need testing with screen readers and other assistive technologies.
accessibilityShortcomingsFooter: These areas are continuously monitored and improved. If you encounter other accessibility issues not listed here, please report them through the feedback channels.
accessibilityTestingBody: The September 2026 review includes source inspection, axe-core page checks, theme and language samples and programmatic interaction tests for dialogs, form errors, navigation, chat, reflow and text spacing. Automated results are evidence for specific checks, not a certification of full accessibility.
accessibilityMonitoringBody: The Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom enforces compliance with accessibility requirements. If you are dissatisfied with the reply you received from Digitaltableteur about a detected accessibility shortcoming or you did not receive a reply within 14 days, you may submit a complaint or request for information to the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom.
accessibilityMonitoringAgency: Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom - Digital Accessibility Supervision Unit
accessibilityPublicationWebsite: This website was published on 6 June 2025.
accessibilityPublicationStatement: This accessibility statement was last reviewed on 27 September 2026.
accessibilityPublicationAct: Act on the Provision of Digital Services (306/2019)
accessibilityFeedbackIntro: Feedback on the accessibility of this website is welcome. If you encounter accessibility barriers or have suggestions for improvement:
accessibilityFeedbackResponse: The aim is to respond to accessibility feedback within 5 business days. Please describe the issue you encountered, including the page URL, your browser and assistive technology (if applicable) and any error messages. Digitaltableteur will work with you to provide the information or service you need in an accessible format.
accessibilityComplaintBody: If Digitaltableteur's response does not resolve an accessibility concern or you receive no response within 14 days, you can contact the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom's digital accessibility supervision service. Guidance is available at www.saavutettavuusvaatimukset.fi.
accessibilityAlternativeBody: If you cannot access certain content or features due to accessibility barriers, please get in touch. Digitaltableteur will provide the information in an alternative format (email, phone, document) or assist you in another way to access the services.
accessibilityContactBody: For questions, requests or concerns about this Accessibility Statement, contact: mail@digitaltableteur.com or +358 45 657 4469

audit.metaTitle: Design System Audit for Product Teams | Digitaltableteur
audit.metaDescription: Find component, token, accessibility and governance gaps in your current design system. Receive severity-ranked findings and a practical 90-day roadmap.
audit.title: Find where your design system is costing the team time
audit.lead: Similar components behave differently. Accessibility defects return in new features. Figma and production disagree about what belongs in the system. A focused audit turns those symptoms into an inventory, severity-ranked findings and a 90-day roadmap.
audit.signalsTitle: Use an audit when the system exists but trust is slipping
signals: Components look similar but behave differently across squads
Accessibility defects return because the pattern is not documented
Design and engineering disagree about what is in the system
Token changes break several applications because naming and ownership are unclear
audit.scope: The work starts from the UI surfaces, components, tokens and patterns your team uses now. A representative sample is reviewed for consistency, accessibility and token use. Ownership, review and release practices are mapped alongside the inventory, so the roadmap separates quick fixes from structural work.
steps: Map live UI surfaces and who owns each pattern family.
Sample important flows for consistency, accessibility and token use.
Rank findings by user impact, rework cost and fix complexity.
Agree on minimum standards and an adoption sequence stakeholders can follow.
deliverables: An inventory of the components, tokens and patterns in use
Severity-ranked findings with effort estimates
A 90-day roadmap separating quick wins from structural fixes
Governance recommendations for RFCs, review and release cadence
audit.investNote: Final scope depends on the number of product surfaces, repositories and teams included.

faq.question: How much of the product does the audit cover?
faq.answer: A representative sample of the surfaces, components, tokens and patterns in use, not every screen. Scope depends on the surfaces, repositories and teams included.

faq.question: Does the audit fix what it finds?
faq.answer: No. It is a decision tool: an inventory, ranked findings and a 90-day roadmap. Fixes can follow as Design System Lift-Off or an embedded partnership.

faq.question: Is this an accessibility conformance audit?
faq.answer: Accessibility is reviewed as part of pattern quality, with WCAG 2.2 AA as the reference. A conformance evaluation or certificate is scoped separately.

audit.bookBody: Talk through the system, the teams involved and what the audit should answer. A calendar invite arrives by email.

uxSprint.metaTitle: UX Sprint: a Tested Prototype in Two Weeks | Digitaltableteur
uxSprint.metaDescription: Two weeks from an open product question to a working prototype of the key flow, an eval plan to test it with users and a handoff your team can build from.
uxSprint.title: Test the riskiest flow before the team builds it
uxSprint.lead: A new flow is about to absorb months of build time and nobody has seen it work. A UX Sprint turns the open question into a working prototype of the key flow, an eval plan to test it with users and a handoff your team can build from.
uxSprint.signalsTitle: Use a sprint when a decision is waiting on evidence
signals: A new feature or flow is about to go into a long build
Stakeholders disagree about how the key flow should work
Usability problems keep surfacing late, after release
An AI feature needs a defined way to judge whether its output is good enough
uxSprint.scope: The sprint focuses on one key flow: the one where the product decision carries the most risk. It is framed with the people who own it, built as a working prototype in your own components where possible and paired with an eval plan that says how users will test it and what counts as success.
steps: Frame the decision, the users and the success criteria with the team that owns the flow.
Map the flow and sketch the alternatives worth testing.
Build a working prototype of the key flow.
Write the eval plan and hand over the prototype, findings and next steps.
deliverables: A working prototype of the key flow
An eval plan with tasks, participants and success criteria
A decision record of the options considered
A handoff your team can build from
uxSprint.investNote: Final scope depends on the complexity of the flow, the number of user groups and how much of your existing design system the prototype can reuse.

faq.question: Is a UX Sprint the same as a design system audit?
faq.answer: No. The sprint answers one product question with a working prototype. The Design System Audit reviews the system you already have and ends in a 90-day roadmap. They are booked separately.

faq.question: Who runs the user tests?
faq.answer: The eval plan is ready for your team or a research partner to run, with tasks, participants and success criteria written out.

faq.question: Can the prototype become production code?
faq.answer: It is built to test the decision, not to ship. Parts built with your design system's components carry over, and Design System Lift-Off or an embedded partnership can take the flow to production.

uxSprint.bookBody: Talk through the flow, the decision it supports and who needs to be involved. A calendar invite arrives by email.

liftoff.metaDescription: Audit, tokens, core components, Storybook and an adoption playbook in four weeks: a design system foundation your teams can build on.
liftoff.title: From scattered components to a system your teams can build on
liftoff.lead: Every squad ships slightly different buttons, forms and modals. Storybook no longer matches production. Lift-Off covers the audit, token architecture, core components, Storybook and an adoption playbook in four weeks.
liftoff.signalsTitle: Use Lift-Off when every squad builds its own version
signals: Every squad ships slightly different buttons, forms and modals
Storybook exists but stories do not match production usage
Figma variables and CSS custom properties use different names
Dark mode is bolted on instead of designed as a theme
liftoff.scope: An audit of the current foundation, then a token taxonomy, the core component set and Storybook documentation, with an adoption playbook for the teams that will use it. Components are prioritised by traffic, rework cost and accessibility risk.
limits: A rebuild of every existing component
Migration of every product to the new system
steps: Prioritise components by traffic, rework cost and accessibility risk.
Define composition patterns before building one-off variants.
Document states, edge cases and keyboard behaviour in Storybook.
Pilot with one product squad, then expand with measured adoption.
deliverables: A token taxonomy from primitive to semantic to component
A core component set with typed props and accessibility baselines
Storybook documentation with usage do's and don'ts
A contribution guide, review checklist and adoption playbook
liftoff.investNote: Final scope depends on the number of components, products and teams included.

faq.question: What do the four weeks include?
faq.answer: An audit of the current foundation, token architecture, core components, Storybook documentation and an adoption playbook.

faq.question: Is every component rebuilt?
faq.answer: No. The core set is chosen by traffic, rework cost and accessibility risk. Composition patterns come before one-off variants.

faq.question: How do teams adopt it?
faq.answer: A pilot with one product squad comes first, then a wider rollout with measured adoption.

faq.question: What happens after the four weeks?
faq.answer: Your team runs the system with the adoption playbook. Continued work can run as an embedded partnership.

liftoff.bookBody: Talk through your products, teams and current components. A calendar invite arrives by email.

aiops.metaDescription: Workflow setup, component governance, AI tooling hooks and a DesignOps playbook your team can run, in three weeks.
aiops.title: Put guardrails and automation around how design work ships
aiops.lead: Reviews bottleneck when headcount does not scale with output. Nobody has defined what agents and tools may change. AI-Ready Ops sets up the workflow, component governance, AI tooling hooks and a DesignOps playbook your team can run, in three weeks.
aiops.signalsTitle: Use it when design debt grows faster than review
signals: Design review bottlenecks when headcount does not scale with output
Handoffs still rely on screenshots and chat threads
No single source of truth for what agents or tools may change
Design debt accumulates faster than manual QA can catch
aiops.scope: A map of where time is lost across spec, build, review and release. Then guardrails for what agents and tools may change in the design system, drift checks in CI and one workflow automated end to end.
limits: Automating decisions that need human judgement
Rolling automation across every workflow at once
steps: Map where time is lost: spec, build, review or release.
Separate safe automation targets from decisions that need human judgement.
Prototype one workflow end to end, for example a token pull request.
Measure throughput and error rate before expanding automation.
deliverables: A DesignOps workflow map with automation candidates
Guardrails for agent and tool changes to the design system
Linting or CI checks for token and component drift
A playbook for human-in-the-loop review
aiops.investNote: Final scope depends on the number of workflows, repositories and teams included.

faq.question: Which workflow is automated first?
faq.answer: One workflow end to end, for example a token pull request or a component scaffold, chosen where time is lost today.

faq.question: Who stays in control?
faq.answer: Your team. The playbook defines what agents and tools may change and which decisions need human review.

faq.question: Which AI tools are used?
faq.answer: Provider selection depends on your stack and policies. The AI use policy describes how AI is used in client work.

faq.question: How is success measured?
faq.answer: Throughput and error rate are measured on the first workflow before automation expands.

aiops.bookBody: Talk through where design work slows down today. A calendar invite arrives by email.

partnership.metaDescription: Senior design and design-system leadership embedded in your team for six or twelve months, at the 90 €/h partnership rate.
partnership.title: Senior design and system leadership, embedded in your team
partnership.lead: For product organisations that need design-system stewardship, governance and hands-on delivery over months rather than weeks. Six or twelve months at four or more days a week, at the 90 €/h partnership rate.
partnership.signalsTitle: Use a partnership when the work outlasts a sprint
signals: An embedded design partner across product and brand
Design system programs with governance and agent-assisted ops
Holistic design leadership for the whole product
Org-wide design system stewardship and AI enablement
partnership.scope: Dedicated design expertise four or more days a week: the complete design process and its deliverables, direct collaboration and strategic design guidance, with specialists from a network added as the work needs them.
limits: Terms under six months at the partnership rate
Fewer than four days a week at the partnership rate
steps: Agree the term, days per week and the outcomes the partnership owns.
Start with a short audit of the current system and team practices.
Work inside your planning, review and release rituals.
Review progress against the agreed outcomes and adjust the plan.
deliverables: Dedicated design expertise four or more days a week
The complete design process and its deliverables
Direct collaboration and strategic design guidance
Specialists from a network when the work needs them
partnership.investMeta: 6 or 12 months, 4 or more days a week
partnership.investNote: Six months at four days a week is 780 hours, about €70k. Shorter terms or lighter weeks use the standard 120 €/h rate.

faq.question: How is the price set?
faq.answer: Hours across the term at 90 €/h, 25% below the standard 120 €/h. Six months at four days a week is 780 hours, about €70k.

faq.question: Can it start smaller?
faq.answer: Yes, at the standard rate. Terms under six months or under four days a week are priced at 120 €/h or as a fixed package.

faq.question: Can the partnership run longer than six months?
faq.answer: Yes. The twelve-month term keeps the 90 €/h partnership rate.

partnership.bookTitle: Plan the partnership on a 30-minute call
partnership.bookBody: Talk through the term, the weekly rhythm and what the partnership should own. A calendar invite arrives by email.

workshop.metaDescription: Two facilitated days on your design system, with prep work before and a written analysis after. Quoted per workshop by group size, travel and format.
workshop.title: Get the team aligned on the design system in two days
workshop.lead: Designers, engineers and product owners describe the same system differently. Decisions stall because nobody owns them. The workshop starts with prep work, works through the hard questions in two facilitated days and ends with a written analysis the team can act on.
workshop.signalsTitle: Use a workshop when the team needs a shared picture
signals: Design and engineering describe the system in different terms
A rebuild, migration or new brand is coming and the plan is unclear
Ownership of components and tokens is undecided
Earlier initiatives started strong and stalled
workshop.scope: Prep work maps the current setup through short interviews and a review of the components, tokens and documentation in use. The two days work through priorities, ownership and next steps with the people who make the decisions. The analysis afterwards records what was agreed and what is still open.
steps: Interview key people and review the current setup before the first day.
Day one: map the system, the people who use it and where it fails them.
Day two: agree on priorities, ownership and a sequence for the next steps.
Deliver a written analysis with findings and a plan for next steps.
deliverables: A summary of the prep interviews and setup review
Workshop outputs captured and cleaned up
A written analysis of findings and open questions
A prioritised plan for next steps
workshop.investNote: Quoted per workshop. The price depends on group size, travel and whether the workshop runs remotely or on-site.

faq.question: Who should take part?
faq.answer: The people who decide how the system is built and used: design, engineering and product leads. Group size affects the format and the quote.

faq.question: Can it run remotely?
faq.answer: Yes. Both remote and on-site delivery are possible. On-site delivery adds travel to the quote.

faq.question: What happens after the two days?
faq.answer: A written analysis and a plan for next steps. Continuing is optional: the plan can feed a UX Sprint, a Lift-Off or work run by your own team.

faq.question: How much preparation does the team need?
faq.answer: A few short interviews and access to the current components, tokens and documentation. The prep work handles the rest.

workshop.bookTitle: Get a quote for your team
workshop.bookBody: Describe the team, the preferred format and what the workshop should answer. The reply covers format, dates and a quote.

designopsPilot.metaDescription: A supervised agent that triages components, keeps tokens honest and drafts release notes your team approves. Ongoing, billed monthly.
designopsPilot.title: Hand routine design system upkeep to a supervised agent
designopsPilot.lead: Component requests pile up. Token values drift between design files and code. Release notes get written last, if at all. DesignOps Pilot runs a supervised agent that triages components, keeps tokens honest and drafts release notes. Your team approves every change.
designopsPilot.signalsTitle: Use it when upkeep crowds out design system work
signals: Component requests wait weeks for triage
Token values drift between design files and code
Release notes are written late or not at all
The core team spends more time on upkeep than on improvements
designopsPilot.scope: The agent works in your existing repositories and tools. It sorts incoming component requests and issues, flags token drift between design and code and drafts release notes from merged changes. Every output goes to your team for approval before anything ships.
steps: Connect the agent to the repositories, trackers and design files in scope.
Agree on what the agent may draft and what always needs approval.
Run triage, drift checks and release note drafts on a regular cadence.
Review the results monthly and adjust scope, rules and guardrails.
deliverables: A configured agent running in your tools
Triage of incoming component requests and issues
Token drift reports between design and code
Release note drafts ready for approval
A monthly review of results and guardrails
designopsPilot.investNote: The monthly price depends on the number of repositories, design files and teams the agent covers.

faq.question: Can the agent change production?
faq.answer: No. The agent drafts and reports. Your team approves every change before it ships.

faq.question: Which tools does it work with?
faq.answer: The repositories, issue trackers and design files your team already uses. Provider selection depends on your stack and policies. The AI use policy describes how AI is used in client work.

faq.question: How long is the commitment?
faq.answer: It runs as an ongoing monthly engagement. Notice terms are agreed in the contract.

faq.question: How is success measured?
faq.answer: Triage time, drift caught before release and the share of drafts approved without rework, reviewed every month.

designopsPilot.bookBody: Talk through where upkeep slows the team down. A calendar invite arrives by email.

agentPilot.metaDescription: Scope one workflow and ship a working agent with guardrails, evals and a handoff your team can run, in three weeks.
agentPilot.title: Ship one working agent with guardrails in three weeks
agentPilot.lead: AI experiments rarely leave the demo stage when nobody has scoped the workflow, the guardrails or who runs the agent afterwards. Agent Pilot picks one workflow, ships a working agent with guardrails and evals and hands it to a team that can run it.
agentPilot.signalsTitle: Use it when AI ideas stall before production
signals: Several agent ideas, none in production
Unclear which workflow is safe to automate first
No way to tell whether the output of an agent is good enough
Concern about agents acting without oversight
agentPilot.scope: One workflow, chosen where repetitive work costs the team the most. The pilot defines what the agent may do, builds it with guardrails, sets up evals that measure output quality and documents how your team runs and improves it.
limits: More than one workflow in the same pilot
Agents acting in production without review
steps: Pick one workflow and define what good output looks like.
Set guardrails: what the agent may read, draft and change.
Build the agent and the evals that measure its output.
Hand over with a runbook and a review of the eval results.
deliverables: A working agent for one workflow
Guardrails written down and enforced
Evals that measure output quality
A handoff and runbook your team can run
agentPilot.investNote: Final scope depends on the workflow, the systems the agent connects to and the review process around it.

faq.question: Which workflow should go first?
faq.answer: One with clear inputs, repetitive steps and a person who can judge the output, for example issue triage or documentation drafts.

faq.question: Who stays in control?
faq.answer: Your team. The guardrails define what the agent may do and which steps need human review.

faq.question: Which AI models are used?
faq.answer: Provider selection depends on your stack and policies. The AI use policy describes how AI is used in client work.

faq.question: What happens after the pilot?
faq.answer: Your team runs the agent with the runbook. Agent Workforce extends the same approach to several workflows.

agentWorkforce.metaDescription: A crew of task-specific agents wired into your stack, with monitoring, fallbacks and a runbook your team owns, in six weeks.
agentWorkforce.title: Run several task-specific agents your team can trust
agentWorkforce.lead: One agent proved the idea. Now several workflows need automation without losing oversight. Agent Workforce wires a crew of task-specific agents into your stack, with monitoring, fallbacks and a runbook your team owns.
agentWorkforce.signalsTitle: Use it when one pilot is not enough
signals: A pilot agent works and more workflows are waiting
Agents need to hand work to each other or to people
Failures must surface before they reach users
The team needs to own and change the agents
agentWorkforce.scope: Several related workflows, each with its own agent and guardrails. Monitoring shows what the agents do, fallbacks route failures to people and the runbook documents how your team operates, changes and retires each agent.
limits: Automating decisions that need human judgement
Platform engineering outside the agreed workflows
steps: Map the workflows and the handoffs between agents and people.
Build each agent with guardrails and evals.
Add monitoring, alerts and fallbacks to human review.
Hand over with a runbook and a joint review of the first runs.
deliverables: A crew of task-specific agents wired into your stack
Monitoring and alerts for agent activity
Fallbacks that route failures to people
A runbook your team owns
agentWorkforce.investNote: Final scope depends on the number of workflows, the systems involved and the monitoring already in place.

faq.question: Is an Agent Pilot needed first?
faq.answer: Not necessarily, but it helps. A pilot proves one workflow before several run together.

faq.question: How are failures handled?
faq.answer: Monitoring flags unusual results and fallbacks route the work to a person instead of guessing.

faq.question: Who owns the agents afterwards?
faq.answer: Your team. The runbook covers how to operate, change and retire each agent.

faq.question: Which AI models are used?
faq.answer: Provider selection depends on your stack and policies. The AI use policy describes how AI is used in client work.

dsMcp.metaDescription: Machine-readable component contracts, an MCP server and an eval benchmark so coding agents build with your design system, in four weeks.
dsMcp.title: Make your design system readable for coding agents
dsMcp.lead: Coding agents already write a share of the UI. Without access to the design system they guess: hardcoded colours, duplicate components, props that do not exist. Design System MCP turns the system into contracts and an MCP server agents can query, then measures how well they use it.
dsMcp.signalsTitle: Use it when agents write UI that ignores the system
signals: Generated code hardcodes values the tokens already define
Agents recreate components that already exist
Component docs are written for people, not for tools
Nobody can say whether agent output follows the system
dsMcp.scope: The components, tokens and usage rules your team already has. Each component gets a machine-readable contract. An MCP server exposes the contracts, tokens and guidance to coding agents in your editors and pipelines. An eval benchmark measures how often agents produce on-system UI, before and after.
limits: Choosing or licensing the coding agents
Rolling the setup out across every repository at once
steps: Inventory the components, tokens and rules agents need to know.
Write machine-readable contracts for the components in scope.
Ship an MCP server and connect it to the editors and agents the team uses.
Benchmark agent output before and after, then hand over.
deliverables: Machine-readable contracts for the components in scope
An MCP server for contracts, tokens and usage guidance
Drift checks that flag where code and contracts disagree
An eval benchmark with before and after results
Documentation for keeping the contracts current
dsMcp.investNote: Final scope depends on the number of components, repositories and agent tools included.

faq.question: What is an MCP server?
faq.answer: A Model Context Protocol server lets AI tools look up information on demand. Here it answers questions about your components, tokens and usage rules.

faq.question: Which coding agents does it work with?
faq.answer: Any tool that supports the Model Context Protocol. The setup is tested with the editors and agents your team uses.

faq.question: Does the design system need to be in good shape first?
faq.answer: It helps. Gaps found while writing the contracts are listed. A Design System Audit can come first when the system needs work.

faq.question: How is success measured?
faq.answer: The eval benchmark runs the same UI tasks before and after and compares how often the output follows the system.

dsMcp.bookBody: Talk through the design system and the agents your team uses. A calendar invite arrives by email.

procurementFaq.title: Buying from Digitaltableteur
procurementFaq.intro: Answers for procurement, legal and finance teams. Anything not covered here can go in the first message.

items.question: Who is the contracting party?
items.answer: Digitaltableteur, a Finnish sole trader registered in the Trade Register. Business ID 2264455-2, VAT ID FI22644552, Hämeentie 8 C 26, 00530 Helsinki.

items.question: Is Digitaltableteur a verified supplier?
items.answer: Yes. Tax, pension and employer obligations are continuously verified through Vastuu Group's Reliable Partner programme, as the Finnish Contractor's Obligations Act requires. The report is public.

items.question: Who does the work?
items.answer: One senior practitioner leads and does the work, with a single point of contact throughout. When an engagement needs more hands, specialists join under subcontract: front-end engineering, accessibility testing, brand and visual design or motion and 3D.

items.question: How is invoicing handled?
items.answer: E-invoices go to address 003722644552 through APIX Messaging Oy, operator ID 003723327487. Payment terms are agreed in the engagement.

items.question: Do prices include VAT?
items.answer: No. Prices exclude Finnish VAT, currently 25.5%.

items.question: Is the work insured?
items.answer: Yes. Liability insurance and legal expenses insurance cover client engagements. A certificate with the coverage limits is available on request.

items.question: Can a client NDA or framework agreement be used?
items.answer: Yes. A short engagement agreement is also available.

items.question: How is personal data handled?
items.answer: A GDPR data processing agreement (DPA) is available on request before work starts.

items.question: Where does the work happen?
items.answer: In your repositories and accounts. Client code and data are not copied elsewhere.

items.question: Who owns the work?
items.answer: You keep full ownership of the code, design and tokens built together. No lock-in, no licensing games.

items.question: Which working languages are available?
items.answer: English, Finnish and Swedish, in workshops and in documentation.

items.question: Is the work remote or on site?
items.answer: Remote by default, based in Helsinki.

items.question: Does the work cover accessibility law?
items.answer: The work targets WCAG 2.2 AA, which includes the WCAG 2.1 AA criteria that EN 301 549 and the European Accessibility Act rely on. A formal conformance evaluation is scoped separately.

items.question: Is AI used on client work?
items.answer: Only as described in the AI use policy, which lists the tools, the safeguards and how client data is handled.
